Summary: Monotheism is belief in one God, and it sets the Bible apart in the ancient world, where every nation had its pantheon. Israel's confession - the LORD our God, the LORD is one - was both theology and loyalty: one God means one allegiance, one Creator, one Judge, one Savior. Christianity holds this confession together with the Trinity: one God in three persons, not three gods, a mystery the church has carefully guarded ever since.
